sentences.text: This application for bail under Section 483 BNSS has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with FIR No.21/2024 registered at Mahila Police Station Sirohi, District Sirohi, for offences under Sections 323, 384, 450 & 376(2)(n) of IPC.

2. Drawing attention of the Court towards the FIR and challan papers, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the prosecutrix, who is a mature woman was in mutual relationship with the present petitioner since 2021.
Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner has been roped in a false criminal case.

3. Drawing attention of the Court towards the various whatsapp chats and photographs of the petitioner and the prosecutrix attached with the case file, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the prosecutrix who is a mature woman and is [2025:RJ-JD:8073] (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-15791/2024] presently working on the post of Constable in Rajasthan Police entered into mutual relationship with present petitioner in the year 2021.

The prosecutrix continued her relationship with present petitioner for about 3 years, however, on relations between them turning Hemant Damor vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:8073) on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155501910/
1 strained, the prosecutrix has roped the petitioner in a false criminal case.

sentences.text: Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody; trial of the case will take sufficiently long time to conclude; therefore, no fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the petitioner behind the bars for an indefinite period.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the petitioner prayed that the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
4. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at Bar.
Perused the material available on record.

6. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that no plausible explanation has been furnished by the prosecutrix for lodging the FIR after an inordinate delay of about three years.

This Court also prima facie finds that the argument of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner and the prosecutrix were having a consensual relationship, however, when their relations came to surface, she has roped the petitioner in a false criminal case, cannot be brushed aside at this stage.

This court also prima facie finds that the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the prosecutrix or fleeing away from justice, in case he is enlarged on bail, thus without expressing any [2025:RJ-JD:8073] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-15791/2024] opinion on merits/demerits of the case
, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

7. Accordingly, the bail application under Section 483 BNSS is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner- Hemant Damor S/o Shri Magan Lal shall be enlarged on bail in connection with FIR No.21/2024 registered at Mahila Police Station Sirohi, District Sirohi provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to so.
